Subject: MAP kickoff — unit-econ sanity checks (tokens/$, caching & batching)

Tom / Sasha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed in the call, the next step on the MAP is a short economics sanity pass focused on production assumptions that will drive procurement sizing and pricing decisions:

- tokens per user/session (baseline + 90th pct)
- expected cache hit rates (session & prefix caching)
- batching assumptions (average batch size / target latency)
- model variants / quantization tradeoffs we should assume for pricing tiers

I've attached a starter MAP workbook (MQ_MAP_v1.xlsx) with the table we usually use to capture these levers. Could you and Sasha fill in approximate targets for 1) tokens/user, 2) expected cache hit, and 3) latency SLAs for the pilot? If you prefer, we can run the numbers with your traffic profile — happy to take a csv export.

Goal: lock on the unit-econ assumptions by EOW Friday so pricing and Dedicated sizing can be finalized for quarter close.

Proposed quick working session: Wed 08/11 10:00 PDT — 30 min — we'll run through the worksheet and produce a 1-page decision record.

Attachments: MQ_MAP_v1.xlsx (Excel, 38KB)

Thanks,

From: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@mediquest.health>

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit-econ sanity checks (tokens/$, caching & batching)

Sergio —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers from our side after a quick sync with Sasha:

- tokens/user: baseline 1,200 tokens per interaction, expected 3,800 tokens per user/day at 95th percentile for heavy clinicians.
- cache hit rate: session-level caching estimate 55% for autocompletion flows; prefix-level reuse across templates ~18%.
- batching: we need median latency <= 350ms; we can tolerate up to 700ms P95 for background summarization flows. For interactive UIs we'll aim for batch sizes of 1–4 (real-time), batchable background jobs up to 16.
- model variants: pilot uses base-1.3B quantized perf model; for prod we expect to evaluate 3B/7B variants if performance/cost warrants.

We'll fill the MQ_MAP_v1.xlsx with the numbers and upload by EOD Wed. Wed 10:00 PDT works for the working session — Tom and Sasha will join.

---
Tom Bennett
Head of Product
MediQuest Health

Sergio / Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up. A few internal comments so we present a crisp ops/econ readout in Wed's session:

- We'll run two scenarios in the workbook: "Conservative" (cache hit 30%, per-token price high) and "Optimistic" (cache hit 60%, batching effective).
- Karthik: please prepare a quick note on latency vs batch-size tradeoffs for the base-1.3B quantized path. Include guidance on expected tokens/sec for 1 GPU with continuous batching + prefix cache enabled.

Also flagging an ask from procurement: if they move to Dedicated we need a 12-month commitment model and a fallback to hosted for overflow — we should be ready to show the cost delta (tokens/$) across both modes.
